Marketers Level Up: The Unignorable Power of the Gamer Economy as ‘GTA VI’ Arrives

Plus, Staples rewards the viral TikTok creator known as the Staples Baddie with a promotion to corporate strategist

By

, WSJ Leadership Institute

Good morning. The long-awaited release of “Grand Theft Auto VI” today is demonstrating the power of gaming with striking force. Its expected multibillion-dollar sales are likely to eclipse the global box office to date for “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” the gross for “Hamilton” on Broadway since 2015, or Comcast’s ad revenue from the 2024 Olympics.

But marketing leaders at the Leadership Institute’s WSJ CMO Council Summit on Wednesday said “GTA VI” is just a more visible example of what gamers already know.

“We can’t sponsor that one, but I love it,” said Visa CMO Frank Cooper III, noting the game’s endemic car theft and vehicular assault.

Visa last spring struck a multiyear partnership deal with Electronic Arts, however, to provide in-game rewards and out-of-game experiences for players of “EA Sports FC” and “EA Sports College Football.”
